content.thinking:
I need to design a frost axe displayed upright on a small ice-block plinth so it touches the floor, keeping it a plain object without joints.

Still planning proportions: haft running vertically above the plinth with the axe head centered partway up, and a crescent blade silhouette extruded sideways so it reads clearly from the front view.

Mapping out the full polygon coordinates now, connecting the top horn through the convex cutting edge, down to the bottom horn, and back along the haft side to close the shape without self-intersection.

For the blade coloring I want a gradient from deep blue near the haft to pale cyan at the edge, with frost cracks generated through cell noise patterns creating thin light lines. I'm also planning a double-bit design with a smaller ice-spike or fin on the opposite side, a spear point on top, and a butt spike anchoring into the plinth, plus glowing rune decals on the blade surface.

I'll add glowing icosahedron gems and icicle shard cones around the head, striped grip wrap, and a pommel, then build a hexagonal lathed plinth with frosted stone and tilted ice crystal shards at the base. Since I can't test the code, I'm sticking to APIs I'm confident about—part, sweep, rod, extrude, lathe, and spike—while being careful about the spike function's overloaded parameters for direction, length, radius, and color.

I'm being careful to only import what I actually use to avoid unused-import errors, planning to use rng, paint, cells, mix, smoothstep, and cel for toon-style coloring on the stone and haft. I'm setting up a root joint and defining the plinth's lathe outline as an octagonal profile with stone-colored paint.

Now I'm building out the ice slab tier above the plinth, sinking the axe butt slightly, then designing the haft as a swept catmull-rom path from the base up to 1.58 units tall with a dark steel-blue grain texture, and planning wrapped grip rings made from small torus segments along the handle.

Next I'm adding the pommel butt cap, collar rings, and planning the socket/collar geometry for mounting the head at the 1.2 height mark, using steel tones with hints of gold or cyan accenting for a frosty, regal look.

Writing socket and spearhead shapes...

That puts the axe 1.65m above the plinth, a touch tall, so I'm scaling the blade outline down by a factor of about 0.72 to bring it to a more realistic 0.78m height with 0.43m reach.

I'm checking that the spear and blade don't overlap in their socket placement, adjusting the spear to start at 1.36 and end at 1.72, and extruding the blade along the correct axis so it sits properly embedded in the socket radius.

Now I'm adding a darker inner inset plate to the blade, a smaller scaled outline offset from center with slightly thicker extrusion, to give it a layered crescent detail with runes inside the main blade shape.

The inner plate at 0.046 thickness slightly protrudes past the main 0.036 plate on each side, adding a bevel effect. For the cutting edge, I'm adding a glowing cyan-white highlight tube that sweeps along the blade's edge curve, slightly inset from the outline with rounded caps.

Now I'm working on decorative runes for the inner plate—placing SVG-based decal planes with cyan strokes, positioning them carefully on the blade surface, and considering how the texture orientation differs between the front-facing and back-facing planes.

I'm sketching three stacked rune glyphs made of chevrons, diamonds, and lines, then moving on to a paint function for frost cracks along the blade. This uses smoothstep across the blade's outline coordinate to blend a base color gradient.

Writing shader logic...

Still writing outline geometry...

For the ice crystal shards, I'm thinking of placing small cones along the blade's top edge using b.part with cone geometry, orienting each by its position and direction to suggest jagged growth.

For the socket, I'm arranging a ring of icicle cones around the base pointing outward and downward, and adding small glowing gem icosahedrons on the front and back bosses for a crystalline accent.

Now I'm adding plinth details: a ring of seven angled crystal cone shards rising from the base, and a thin bluish ice slab beneath the plinth to suggest frost on the ground.

Still writing geometry...

I'm rotating the rings so their normals align with Y, alternating 16 colors with gold bands at the collar points, then adding a hanging ribbon tassel by sweeping a tapered outline off the grip's side.

For the ribbon's orientation, I'm checking its thickness runs along the cross of z and y, placing it just outside the rod's radius so it doesn't clip. I'll paint it with a solid color plus a gold stripe based on its local height coordinate, and reuse a similar coordinate-based paint technique for the spearhead blade.

For the blade, I'm shading faces white when nearly perpendicular to z, otherwise blending between deep and icy tones based on vertical position, with the thickness axis running along x instead. I'll add a small cluster of frost crystal cones at the socket-blade junction, angled outward, to finish off the detail without overdoing it.

Now I'm adding dark rivets as small spheres around the socket flange and gold rivets at the plate corners on the blade face, keeping the part count modest. For the rune glow, I'm defining a plane with a texture at the center of the inner plate, positioning it just above the bevel so the glowing rune sits flush on the flat face.

Checking the plane placement at z=0.027 against the plate's half-thickness of 0.023 to make sure it sits correctly, and confirming the 0.13x0.26 rectangle fits within the plate's u/v bounds on both the front and back faces, mirroring the glow plane on the spike side as well. Setting up a scale helper and typed outline points to build the geometry consistently...

Still writing helper types...

Working through smoothing settings and bevel limits for the blade extrusion, making sure bevel stays under half the thickness, and sorting out parameter naming for the paint and cell functions before writing out the actual file.

Writing shard geometry helpers...

Adding small gold rivets to the head plate at specific offset points, plus edge glow accents along the plate and spike, before finalizing the geometry.
